quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #22
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the highway angles toward the center. What does this mean?

options.text: You are approaching a construction area.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is getting narrower.
questions.explanation: A solid line on the side of the road marks the edge. When this line angles toward the center, the road is narrowing ahead.

questions.question: What do pentagonal signs indicate?
questions.correctAnswerText: School zones.
questions.explanation: Pentagonal signs mark school zones. Watch for children and pedestrians near schools.

questions.question: When must you pull over for an emergency vehicle?

options.text: No matter which direction it is coming from.
Only if it is behind you.
Only if it is coming toward you.

questions.correctAnswerText: No matter which direction it is coming from.
questions.explanation: Pull over to the right edge and stop for any emergency vehicle with flashing lights, whether it is behind you or coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: You are on a narrow road and see an oncoming vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Pull completely off the road and stop.
Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the road.
Demand the other vehicle pull over.
Turn on your high beams so they see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the road.
questions.explanation: On narrow roads, you must leave at least half the road for oncoming traffic. Both vehicles need space to pass safely.

questions.question: About how much alcohol does your body process per hour?
questions.correctAnswerText: One drink.
questions.explanation: The average person processes about one alcoholic drink per hour. How drunk you get depends on how much you drink, how fast you drink it, and your weight, food intake, and health.

questions.question: What helps direct drivers into the correct lanes for turning on highways?

options.text: White lines on the side of the road.
White arrows in the middle of lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows in the middle of lanes.
questions.explanation: Arrows in lanes show which direction you should go, such as straight or turning.

questions.question: The light is green and you want to turn left, but traffic is heavy. What should you do?

options.text: Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.
Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
Turn since you have a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
questions.explanation: You may enter the intersection on green, but wait in the center for oncoming traffic to pass before turning left. Never force your way if traffic is coming.

questions.question: You are in traffic crossing railroad tracks with no signals or gates. What should you do?

options.text: You have the right-of-way and don't need to check for trains.
You may pass slower drivers while crossing.
Make sure your vehicle has room to cross completely without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle has room to cross completely without stopping.
questions.explanation: Check that you have enough space to cross the tracks without stopping. Never pass another car at a railroad crossing. Always look for trains before crossing tracks.

questions.question: The traffic light turns yellow as you approach an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Treat it like a caution sign and continue through.
Stop before the intersection, unless stopping would be unsafe.
Speed up to get through before the red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before the intersection, unless stopping would be unsafe.
questions.explanation: Slow down and stop before entering on yellow if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop, drive carefully through.

questions.question: Your car has Anti-Lock Brakes and loses traction on a slippery road. What should you do?

options.text: Press and hold the brake pedal.
Press and hold the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Press hard on the brake pedal and hold it. Steer away from danger. The Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) pumps the brakes automatically faster than you can. Letting up or pumping the brakes will turn off the ABS.

questions.question: When can you cross double solid yellow lines?
questions.correctAnswerText: To turn into a driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left onto a highway, turn into or out of a driveway, or make a U-turn (if allowed).

questions.question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, what should you do first?
questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: First, take your foot off the gas pedal. If you need to slow down more, gently press the brake pedal slowly and steadily.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in fog?
questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: Before turning left, you must:

options.text: Move to the right side of your lane.
Wait for oncoming traffic to get a red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let oncoming vehicles pass first.
questions.explanation: When turning left at a traffic light, you must let pedestrians and oncoming traffic pass first.

questions.question: What color are signs for public recreation areas?
questions.correctAnswerText: Brown.
questions.explanation: Brown signs show areas of history, culture, or public recreation. They help drivers find places of interest in unfamiliar areas.

questions.question: Your car takes longer to stop on:
questions.correctAnswerText: Wet or icy roads.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance increases on wet or icy roads, as well as on roads covered with loose gravel or stones.

questions.question: What do round signs mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: Round signs warn you that a railroad crossing is coming. Be extra careful when you see this sign.

questions.question: If an oncoming car is heading toward you in your lane, what should you do?

options.text: Honk, turn right, and speed up.
Honk, turn left, and slow down.
Honk, turn right, and slow down.
Stay in your lane, honk, and slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk, turn right, and slow down.
questions.explanation: First, honk to get the other driver's attention. If they do not move, steer to the right. Do not turn left—if the other driver corrects at the last second, you will still crash. Brake hard and steadily. Slowing down even a little will reduce the impact.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, you must:

options.text: Keep driving at your normal speed.
Stop and look for police cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: Unless a sign says you cannot, you may turn right or left at a steady green light. But you must let other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection pass first.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A crossroad is coming. Watch for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: A crossroad is coming. Watch for traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is ahead.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalk, where should a pedestrian walk?

options.text: On the side with the least traffic.
On the same side as traffic moving in that direction.
On the side facing oncoming traffic.
On the side with the most traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Walk on the side of the road that faces the traffic coming toward you.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a hill or incline with a curb, which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Turn them sharply toward the curb.
Turn them slightly to the right.
Turn them sharply away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn them sharply away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels sharply away from the curb. This keeps your car from rolling into traffic if it starts to move downhill. On a street with no curb, turn your wheels toward the edge of the road instead.

questions.question: When must you yield to other drivers?

options.text: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
When a car on your left reaches an unmarked intersection at the same time as you.
When your traffic signal is a green arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
questions.explanation: You must yield to other drivers when entering a street from an alley, driveway, or garage. You must also yield to pedestrians on the sidewalk.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Low ground railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a low ground railroad crossing. The tracks cross the road at a steep angle. Low vehicles may drag or get stuck on the tracks.

questions.question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, which way should you turn your wheels?
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn them to the right.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels sharply toward the side of the road when parking downhill. If your car rolls, it will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Road hazard sign.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs are usually yellow (or orange in work zones). They warn you of a hazard or a place where special rules apply.

questions.question: What color are road markings that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions.

questions.question: You are waiting in an intersection to turn left. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights to ask other drivers to let you through.
Drive around a car blocking you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn. If another car hits you from behind, straight wheels prevent you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this black and yellow sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right is one-way traffic only.
There is a detour to the right due to road work.
Slow down because the road turns sharply.
There is a crossroad to your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down because the road turns sharply.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead makes a sharp turn. Slow down before the curve, just as you would at an intersection.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow arrow traffic signal?

options.text: Merge in the direction of the arrow.
Slow down and stop if you can do so safely.
Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
You have the right-of-way and oncoming traffic must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow means a red arrow is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: What does a speed restriction sign show?

options.text: It can be ignored in rain, snow, or ice.
It is blue with black letters.
It shows the safe speed for a curve or turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: It shows the safe speed for a curve or turn.
questions.explanation: Curves and turns have advisory speed signs. These signs show the recommended speed for driving safely through curves and turns. You should follow these speeds, especially in bad weather like rain, snow, or ice.

questions.question: What should car drivers know about large trucks?

options.text: They can stop faster than cars.
They need the same space to turn as cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have large blind spots.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have blind spots in front, on the sides, and in the back. Do not drive in these areas. Because of their size and weight, trucks need more space to turn and stop than cars.

questions.question: When turning left from a multilane, one-way street or highway, which lane should you start from?
questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane.
questions.explanation: Always start left turns from the left lane on multilane streets and highways.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, what should you do after setting the parking brake?

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Keep the front tires straight ahead.
Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
Turn your steering wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill by a curb, set the parking brake and turn your wheels away from the curb. If your car rolls, it will roll into the curb and stop.

questions.question: If two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
The car on the right must yield to the car on the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at the same time at an uncontrolled intersection, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The left driver can go when it is safe.
